title: Port-convention source registry (per-maker TOML)
description: Schema for the per-maker files in docs/port_convention_sources/ (everything except overlay.toml and waves.toml, which have their own schemas). Enforced by scripts/check_registry_schema.py, which is chained from sync_port_conventions.py --check. `additionalProperties: false` is the point of this file: these rows are hand-authored, nothing validates a key name at load time, and sync_port_conventions._gate reads every field with .get() -- so a typo'd `fetchd` silently reads as not-fetched and skips the row, which is the same silent-skip failure #335 was written to close. See README.md for the prose schema.

name.description: Display name; matches the board JSON's name. Unique across the whole registry.

files.description: Every boards/ JSON this row applies to, as a path relative to boards/.

status.description: verified = at least one fetched source plausibly for this exact board; candidate = a real lead not fetch-verified; none-found = no lead located (queries listed in notes); not-attempted = not yet researched.

notes.description: History + caveats; for none-found, the queries tried.

source.description: Ranked pointers, rank 1 = most authoritative. Absent for none-found / not-attempted rows.

then.description: A verified row must point at something; otherwise nothing was verified.

rank.description: 1 = most authoritative. Ranks must be consecutive from 1 within a board (checked by the validator, not expressible here).

kind.description: Trust tier, descending. vendor-manual marks documentation that authoritatively answers polarity/pin questions without being a constraint file.

format.description: Only the constraint-file formats with a parser under scripts/port_convention_parsers/ can generate a block; the rest make the trust gate skip the row before it attempts a fetch, which is the intended shape for an offline vendor source (a CD archive with no addressable raw URL).

fetched.description: true ONLY if the content was actually retrieved and inspected. Load-bearing: the trust gate refuses to generate from an unfetched rank-1.

evidence.description: Strings matched VERBATIM against the fetched source -- quote the source's own bytes, never a translation (see README).

naming.description: Vouches that a community-hosted source nevertheless uses vendor-canonical port names, which lets the trust gate accept it.

then.description: A canonical-naming vouch must say how it was established -- it unlocks the trust gate.
